## Physical & cycle counts (PLAN 5.4, D-038)

A **stock count** captures the warehouse team's *counted* quantity per `(item, bin, lot)`, compares
it to system on-hand, and posts the differences. Two tables: `inv_stock_counts` (the count document —
`DocumentMixin` + a gapless `CNT-` number claimed at creation, `count_type`, `warehouse_id`,
`status`, `count_date`) and `inv_stock_count_lines` (one line per in-scope quant — `system_qty`
snapshot, `counted_qty`, and, filled at post, `variance_qty` / `adjustment_move_id` / `unit_cost`).

**Physical vs cycle.** A `PHYSICAL` count snapshots **every** quant in the warehouse; a `CYCLE` count
snapshots only the chosen `item_ids` / `bin_ids` (the recurring spot count). The type only changes
which quants are enumerated into lines — the post path is identical for both.

**The flow: snapshot → count → post.** `POST /api/v1/inventory/stock-counts` creates the count
(`DRAFT`) and snapshots one line per in-scope quant with `system_qty` = current on-hand and
`counted_qty` NULL. `POST /stock-counts/{id}/lines/{line}/count` records a counted quantity and moves
the count to `COUNTING`. `GET /stock-counts/{id}/variance-preview` shows per-line live-system vs
counted vs variance vs estimated value impact before posting. `POST /stock-counts/{id}/post` posts
the variances; `POST /stock-counts/{id}/cancel` abandons a `DRAFT`/`COUNTING` count.

**Variance posts via an ADJUSTMENT move, never a bespoke journal (D-038).** For each line the post
computes `variance = counted − live-system`; a non-zero variance posts ONE stock **ADJUSTMENT** move
through `stock_moves.create_move` (positive → ADJUSTMENT *into* the bin, negative → *out of* it). That
move runs the 5.3 costing engine and publishes `StockValued`, so the price-difference journal posts
via the event bus **in the same transaction** — the count inherits every costing/GL/audit invariant
for free. The count's document is linked to each adjustment move via docflow (`counts`), so the
DocFlow viewer renders count → adjustment-move → journal. A **zero-variance** line posts no move
(`adjustment_move_id` stays NULL). The positive-adjustment **unit cost** is sourced from
`queries.current_unit_cost` (the moving-average `avg_unit_cost`, or the FIFO live-layer weighted
average — the same book cost a value-neutral transfer carries), so the value added matches the book
cost; an item the system thinks is empty enters at cost 0 (a quantity-only correction).

**`system_qty` is re-validated at post (D-038 concurrency safety).** The `system_qty` snapshot is only
the *preview* baseline; `post_count` **re-reads live on-hand** for each line as the authoritative
system quantity, so a move that lands between snapshot and post can never post a wrong variance — the
resulting on-hand always equals the *counted* quantity, not `counted − stale`.

**Closed-period interaction.** The whole post runs in `run_in_uow`, so every variance move's costing
journal + the count commit as one transaction. A **closed-period `count_date`** makes the
adjustment's journal trip the period trigger inside that transaction, rolling the **whole** post back
— the count stays unposted (D-018).

**`POSTED` is terminal.** A posted count is never re-posted (the status guard rejects re-post — no
double adjustment, D-013) and never cancelled; corrections are new counts/adjustments (the
append-only ledger philosophy). Posting requires **every** line to be counted (else 422).

**Large counts run as a background job (PERFORMANCE §3).** A post whose snapshot shows more than
`COUNT_POST_SYNC_MAX_VARIANCES` (200) variance lines is submitted as an `inventory.count_post` job
and returns `202 {job_id}` for `/api/v1/jobs` polling; at or below it the post runs inline (200) —
mirroring the depreciation-run (100) / bank-import (1000) thresholds. The job handler delegates to the
same `post_count` engine, so the re-validation and one-transaction guarantee hold off-request too.

Permissions: `inventory.count.read` (the GETs), `inventory.count.manage` (create / record-count /
cancel), `inventory.count.post` (the privileged post — it changes on-hand AND posts GL journals).

42	- **D-037 Inventory costing (PLAN 5.3): valuation is per (item, warehouse); the move ledger + quants are the quantity SSOT, valuation/layers are the value SSOT, all updated in ONE transaction; COGS posts via the event bus in that same transaction:** Which engine a `(item, warehouse)` uses is the item's `costing_method` (MOVING_AVERAGE | FIFO), defaulted from its category. **Moving average** — `inv_item_valuations` (UNIQUE(tenant,item,warehouse), `CHECK(on_hand_qty >= 0)`) holds `on_hand_qty`, full-precision `avg_unit_cost`, `total_value`, locked `with_for_update` (PG row lock; SQLite FOR-UPDATE no-op + single-writer lock, D-020): receipt adds `qty×unit_cost` and recomputes `avg = total_value/on_hand` **unrounded**; issue subtracts `quantize(qty×avg, currency dp, HALF_UP)` and, when on_hand hits **exactly 0**, **flushes the residual `total_value` to the price-difference account** so value and quantity never disagree (the rounding-drift absorber — value lands at exactly 0 even for non-terminating averages). **FIFO** — `inv_cost_layers` (one per receipt, `CHECK(0 <= remaining_qty <= original_qty)`) consumed oldest-first by `(received_at, created_at, id)` under `with_for_update` (created_at is the insertion-order tiebreaker when dates tie — uuid4 ids are not monotonic), with one `inv_layer_consumptions` row per touched layer (the per-layer COGS audit trail AND the **exact-reversal** record). **Cost input:** `inv_stock_moves.unit_cost` (MoneyType nullable, batch-added) — RECEIPT/positive-ADJUSTMENT REQUIRE it (the entry cost); ISSUE/negative-ADJUSTMENT IGNORE it and the engine computes/writes it back; TRANSFER carries the current valuation. **Same-transaction COGS (the inventory↔finance seam, D-011/D-020):** `create_move` updates valuation/layers right after the quant update, then `publish(StockValued(...))` (buffered) carrying the value Δ, the three GL account ids (inventory/COGS/price-difference, opaque per D-029) AND the **chosen offset account** (ISSUE→COGS, RECEIPT/ADJUSTMENT→price-difference, reversal→the opposite of the original's offset); `run_in_uow` drains it before commit and `finance/handlers.py` (the **first real cross-module handler**) posts the journal **through the finance posting service** (`create_draft_entry` + `post_entry`, never raw inserts) in the shared session — so one commit = move + quant + valuation + journal + docflow `posts` link, and **any handler failure rolls the whole transaction back** (a stock move can never exist without its journal entry). The COGS journal posts with `move_date`, so a move dated into a **closed period** fails (the period trigger fires in the same transaction → the move rolls back; you cannot move stock into a closed period — correct by construction). **Postings:** RECEIPT/ADJUSTMENT-up Dr inventory / Cr price-difference (standalone offset; procurement GR overrides later, 6.x); ISSUE Dr COGS / Cr inventory; ADJUSTMENT-down Dr price-difference / Cr inventory; **TRANSFER within one inventory account is value-neutral → NO event, NO journal**; a reversal posts the exact reverse of the original's entry. **Reversal is replay, not recompute:** reversing an ISSUE replays its consumptions backward onto the exact layers / re-adds MAV value at the original cost; reversing a RECEIPT zeros its layer (only if unconsumed, else error) / removes MAV value. **Read surface:** `GET /stock-valuations` + `GET /items/{id}/cost-layers` (permission `inventory.valuation.read`); `queries.item_value`/`valuation_summary` for the inventory-value KPI sum qty×cost in **Python** (typed Decimals), never `func.sum(qty×cost)` — two scaled-integer columns multiply to ×10^12 on SQLite which MoneyType cannot un-scale (D-015 discipline). **Structure:** costing service split into `costing.py` (orchestration), `costing_mav.py`, `costing_fifo.py`, `costing_reversal.py` (all <400 lines); handler registered at the app factory `register_event_handlers` (the deterministic D-011 seam, re-runnable + idempotent so the test harness re-registers after `clear_subscriptions`). Migration `0022_inventory_costing` creates three tables + batch-adds `unit_cost` to non-trigger-bearing `inv_stock_moves`, reversible, zero autogen drift; the `CHECK`s + `with_for_update` proven on real Postgres by the `-m pg` guard tests.

### Variance-posting mechanism
A count line becomes an adjustment move in `post_count`: per line it re-reads live on-hand, computes `variance = counted − live`, and for a non-zero variance posts **one** `ADJUSTMENT` move via `stock_moves.create_move` (positive → `to_bin`, negative → `from_bin`). That existing call already runs the 5.3 costing engine and publishes `StockValued`, so the price-difference journal posts via the event bus **in the same transaction** — no bespoke journal is ever written. The count's document is linked to each move via docflow (`counts`); zero-variance lines post no move (`adjustment_move_id` NULL). The **positive-adjustment unit cost** is sourced from `queries.current_unit_cost` — the moving-average `avg_unit_cost`, or the FIFO live-layer weighted average (the same book cost a value-neutral transfer carries), so value added matches book cost; an item the system thinks is empty enters at cost 0.

### system_qty re-validation
The stored `system_qty` is only the preview baseline. `post_count` re-reads **live** on-hand at post time as the authoritative system qty, so a move landing between snapshot and post can't post a wrong variance — verified by a test: snapshot at 10, count 15, a concurrent +8 receipt lands → posted variance is `15−18=−3` (not `15−10=+5`) and on-hand ends at exactly 15 (the counted qty).

### Background-job path
**Implemented** (not deferred), mirroring 4.9/4.10: the post endpoint returns `202 {job_id}` for an `inventory.count_post` job above 200 snapshot-variance lines, inline `200` at or below — the depreciation/bank-import threshold precedent. `count_jobs.py` delegates to the same `post_count` engine.
